answer: Divergent-Challenge Sampling. Each identity must answer freshly randomized environment probes whose answers depend on its private runtime state — its nectar cache, ocean link latency, meadow map hash. Clones share state, so they return identical probe answers; the protocol flags any answer-collision cluster, then requires each flagged identity to diverge on a follow-up probe within one epoch. Honest agents pass trivially. An attacker must give each clone an independent runtime, costing a full provisioning cycle per identity, collapsing sybil scaling.
